I need the front end for Reelentry. A festival submission service where independent filmmakers, many of them weekend hobbyists, pay entry fees to send their films to festivals and can withdraw entries under each festival's refund rules.

Who's using it: Marcus Bell, a high-school chemistry teacher who spent two summers making a 9-minute short film, 'Low Tide at Gray's', with friends. This is his first time submitting to festivals. He's paying out of his own pocket and has set himself a $250 budget for the season.

What they're doing right now: It's Saturday evening and several early-bird deadlines close at midnight Sunday. He has already paid for three submissions. He's now deciding which of eleven more festivals to commit to. Two of them require a regional premiere, so entering one could disqualify him from the other. One fee waiver code he was emailed still has to be applied. He also wants to withdraw an entry he made impulsively last week to a large festival with a 2% acceptance rate. Its refund window closes in 26 hours and the refund is 50% of the fee. He needs to see what's committed, what each new entry costs, and what can still be undone.

Three paid submissions: Tidewater Shorts ($30, accepted for review), Grain & Lens ($25) and the Halcyon International Film Festival ($55, withdrawable for $27.50 until Sunday 11:59 pm). One unused waiver code, MARSH25, worth $25 at Saltmarsh Film Weekend. Spent so far: $110 of the $250 budget. Payment card on file ending 4471.
